For a fixed x with n+1 > ‖x‖, the open ball centered at x of radius n+1−‖x‖ lies in the plateau. Hence f_n and f agree there, and genuine Fréchet derivatives and Riesz gradients agree at x. Both factors really are differentiable (indeed the cutoff is smooth and f is C²). Mere pointwise value convergence would not suffice. Independently, the product rule and A/(n+1) give gradient convergence even without the plateau argument, if pointwise cutoff convergence is justified.

The mass estimate is 0 ≤ χ² f² ≤ f² ∈ L¹. For a = χ² and q = f² the identity Φ(aq) = aΦ(q) + qΦ(a) holds for positive a,q by log additivity and for a=0 or q=0 by the extension. The convex tangent lower bound a−1 ≤ Φ(a) and Φ(a) ≤ 0 on [0,1] give |Φ(aq)| ≤ |Φ(q)| + q ∈ L¹. The signed estimate alone is insufficient, and q=1 with 0<a<1 refutes |Φ(aq)| ≤ |Φ(q)|.

The genuine product rule and the Riesz isometry give ‖∇f_n‖ ≤ ‖∇f‖ + A|f|, since n+1 ≥ 1, yielding the integrable bound 2‖∇f‖² + 2A² f². Both L² assumptions are used. Continuity of f_n, its gradient and zero-extended Φ gives continuous real scalar integrands, hence Borel measurable and strongly (thus a.e. strongly) measurable because the codomain is ℝ. This does not assert strong measurability of a general E-valued continuous map in a nonseparable E. The L² premise for ∇f separately has a.e. strong measurability, and no vector Bochner integral of ∇f_n is needed.

The three genuine integrable envelopes and pointwise limits justify three scalar dominated-convergence applications on arbitrary measures, even when not σ-finite. Finite dimension enters the downstream compact-smooth test application only: the closed bounded support ball becomes compact, while smoothness of the downstream f is a separate premise.
